## Statement

Let $p\ge1$ be an integer, $T>0$, $h=T/N\le h_0\le1$, and $t_n=nh$. The state dimension $d$ and parameter dimension $m$ are fixed. All vector norms are Euclidean and all matrix norms are their induced operator norms; gradients are columns.

Consider the continuous objective
$$J(\theta)=\phi(u(T,\theta),\theta)+\int_0^T\ell(t,u(t,\theta),\theta)\,dt,$$
and the actual finite graph
$$x_{n+1}=\Psi_n(x_n,\theta),\qquad J_h(\theta)=\phi_h(x_N,\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}L_n(x_n,\theta).$$
Assume the hypotheses of the continuous flow-tangent and adjoint-gradient results hold on a common tube. Write $\Phi_n(x,\theta)$ for the exact flow from $t_n$ to $t_{n+1}$ and
$$K_n(x,\theta)=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\ell(t,u(t;t_n,x,\theta),\theta)\,dt.$$
These exact maps and the actual numerical maps are $C^1$ on open neighborhoods of the admitted state and parameter sets. For every relevant $n$, all states $x_n,u(t_n)$ and the segment joining them belong to a convex admitted state set. All estimates below hold uniformly on those sets and a fixed parameter neighborhood, independently of $N,n$.

For $r=e,h$, define
$$A_n^e=D_x\Phi_n,\quad B_n^e=D_\theta\Phi_n,\quad c_n^e=D_xK_n^T,\quad d_n^e=D_\theta K_n^T,$$
$$A_n^h=D_x\Psi_n,\quad B_n^h=D_\theta\Psi_n,\quad c_n^h=D_xL_n^T,\quad d_n^h=D_\theta L_n^T.$$
Suppose constants $c_v,c_1,L,M,H\ge0$ satisfy, at each admitted $(x,\theta)$,
$$\|\Psi_n-\Phi_n\|\le c_vh^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^h-A_n^e\|,\ \|B_n^h-B_n^e\|,\ \|c_n^h-c_n^e\|,\ \|d_n^h-d_n^e\|\le c_1h^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^r\|\le1+Lh,\qquad \|B_n^r\|,\ \|c_n^r\|,\ \|d_n^r\|\le Mh.$$
Each of $A_n^e,B_n^e,c_n^e,d_n^e$ is Lipschitz in $x$, with constant at most $Hh$.

Let $S_0=D_\theta u(0,\theta)$ and $S_0^h=D_\theta x_0(\theta)$. Assume
$$\|x_0-u(0)\|\le c_0h^p,\qquad \|S_0^h-S_0\|\le c_{s0}h^p,\qquad \|S_0\|\le M_0.$$
The terminal costs are $C^1$. The exact columns $D_x\phi^T,D_\theta\phi^T$ have norm at most $M_\phi$ and are Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $H_\phi$; at the same admitted $(x,\theta)$,
$$\|D_x\phi_h^T-D_x\phi^T\|,\ \|D_\theta\phi_h^T-D_\theta\phi^T\|\le C_\phi h^p.$$
No terminal value-error hypothesis is needed for the gradient conclusion.

Let $S_n^h=D_\theta x_n$, and let $p_n^h$ be the exact discrete adjoint of this numerical graph. Let $S(t)=D_\theta u(t)$ and let $p(t)$ be the continuous adjoint with terminal value $D_x\phi(u(T),\theta)^T$. Define
$$E=e^{LT},\quad X=E(c_0+Tc_v),\quad \overline S=E(M_0+TM),\quad \overline P=E(M_\phi+TM),$$
$$R=c_1+HX,\quad C_S=E\{c_{s0}+TR(\overline S+1)\},\quad D=C_\phi+H_\phi X,$$
$$C_P=E\{D+TR(\overline P+1)\},$$
$$C_G=D+c_{s0}\overline P+(M_0+c_{s0})C_P+T\{R(1+\overline P)+MC_P\}.$$
Then
$$\max_n\|x_n-u(t_n)\|\le Xh^p,\qquad \max_n\|S_n^h-S(t_n)\|\le C_Sh^p,$$
$$\max_n\|p_n^h-p(t_n)\|\le C_Ph^p,\qquad \|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|\le C_Gh^p.$$
These conclusions assume local value and first-derivative consistency, rather than a global adjoint-error estimate. They require no representation by nonnegative quadrature weights.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The common-tube flow result gives the actual parameter derivative and its variational equation. The chain rule gives derivatives of compositions of exact or numerical step maps.

[F2] The continuous adjoint pairing identity integrates on each subinterval. The continuous gradient formula and the finite-graph reverse recursion use column gradients.

[F3] A recurrence $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$ has a uniform order-$p$ bound. The looser bound $e^{LT}(C_0+TC)h^p$ is valid also when $L=0$. The same argument applies after reversing a finite index sequence.

[A1] All domains, differentiability, tube, local consistency, stability, Lipschitz, initial-data and terminal-derivative assumptions in the Statement hold uniformly.

## Proof

1.1 The exact objective is also the finite graph with maps $\Phi_n$, costs $K_n$, initial state $u(0)$ and terminal cost $\phi$: the intervals partition the integral. Differentiability of $K_n$ follows by differentiating its integral using the common-tube flow derivative and the uniform continuous derivative bounds. In particular the initial-state variational matrix $V$ on interval $n$ has $V(t_n)=I$, $V'=f_uV$, and
$$c_n^e=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}V(t)^T\ell_u(t)^T\,dt.$$
The pairing identity gives
$$p(t_n)=c_n^e(u(t_n),\theta)+A_n^e(u(t_n),\theta)^Tp(t_{n+1}).$$
Thus the exact-flow graph adjoint equals the continuous adjoint at every node. Its tangent and gradient are also those of the exact continuous objective. [F1, F2, A1]

1.2 Write $u_n=u(t_n)$ and $e_n=\|x_n-u_n\|$. The derivative bound for $\Psi_n$, integrated along the admitted segment, gives its Lipschitz constant $1+Lh$. Consequently
$$e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+c_vh^{p+1}.$$
By [F3], $e_n\le Xh^p$. [A1, F1, F3]

2.1 The exact tangent and adjoint recurrences give
$$\|S_{n+1}\|\le(1+Lh)\|S_n\|+Mh,\qquad \|p(t_n)\|\le(1+Lh)\|p(t_{n+1})\|+Mh.$$
Expanding these finite recurrences and using $(1+Lh)^k\le e^{LT}$ shows $\|S_n\|\le\overline S$ and $\|p(t_n)\|\le\overline P$. These bounds include $L=0$. For any one of the four derivative maps, comparison at numerical and exact nodes gives
$$\|F_n^h(x_n,\theta)-F_n^e(u_n,\theta)\|\le c_1h^{p+1}+Hh e_n\le Rh^{p+1}.$$
[A1, step 1.2, F3]

3.1 The actual differentiated numerical graph satisfies $S_{n+1}^h=A_n^h(x_n)S_n^h+B_n^h(x_n)$. Subtract the exact recurrence and split the matrix product using $A_n^h(S_n^h-S_n)+(A_n^h-A_n^e)S_n$. Hence
$$\|S_{n+1}^h-S_{n+1}\|\le(1+Lh)\|S_n^h-S_n\|+R(\overline S+1)h^{p+1}.$$
The initial derivative bound and [F3] yield $C_Sh^p$. [F1, A1, step 2.1]

4.1 At the terminal node, the difference of adjoint seeds is at most $Dh^p$. Subtract the two backward recurrences, splitting $A_h^Tp_h-A_e^Tp_e=A_h^T(p_h-p_e)+(A_h-A_e)^Tp_e$. The Euclidean operator norm of a transpose equals that of the matrix; this follows from Cauchy–Schwarz and $\|v\|=\sup_{\|w\|=1}|w^Tv|$. Therefore
$$\|p_n^h-p(t_n)\|\le(1+Lh)\|p_{n+1}^h-p(t_{n+1})\|+R(\overline P+1)h^{p+1}.$$
Reverse the indices and apply [F3]. This gives $C_Ph^p$. [F2, A1, step 2.1]

5.1 Apply the finite-graph gradient formula to both graphs:
$$\nabla J_h=D_\theta\phi_h(x_N)^T+(S_0^h)^Tp_0^h+\sum_{n<N}\{d_n^h(x_n)+(B_n^h(x_n))^Tp_{n+1}^h\},$$
$$\nabla J=D_\theta\phi(u_N)^T+S_0^Tp(0)+\sum_{n<N}\{d_n^e(u_n)+(B_n^e(u_n))^Tp(t_{n+1})\}.$$
The terminal direct-derivative difference is at most $Dh^p$. The initial contribution is bounded by
$$\{c_{s0}\overline P+(M_0+c_{s0})C_P\}h^p,$$
since $h\le1$ implies $\|S_0^h\|\le M_0+c_{s0}$. Each running difference is bounded by
$$\{R+R\overline P+MC_P\}h^{p+1},$$
using $B_h^T(p_h-p)+(B_h-B_e)^Tp$. Summing $N$ terms and using $Nh=T$ proves the stated $C_G$ bound. [F2, steps 1.1, 2.1, 4.1, A1] ∎

## Statement

Use the dimensions, exact interval maps $\Phi_n,K_n$, terminal and initial data, and Euclidean conventions of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]]. Let $(A,b,c)$ be a fixed explicit $s$-stage tableau with $c_i=\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}$ and $\sum_i b_i=1$. Its weights may be negative or zero. The actual numerical state and cost maps are
$$Y_i=x+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}f(t_n+c_jh,Y_j,\theta),$$
$$\Psi_n=x+h\sum_i b_if(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta),\qquad L_n=h\sum_i b_i\ell(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta).$$
These are exact finite-stage maps, not outputs of a stopped implicit solver.

Assume $f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^d$ and $\ell:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ are $C^2$ on an open convex time-state-parameter domain. On a common compact convex subset with positive margin in $\mathcal D$, their derivatives through order two are uniformly bounded. All admitted local exact trajectories, all numerical trajectories and stages, and all needed joining segments lie in this domain and common tube, uniformly over the fixed parameter neighborhood and $h\le h_0$. Stage times outside $[t_n,t_{n+1}]$ are included when the tableau has such abscissae. Unique admitted local flows are assumed as in the flow-tangent supplier.

Put $r=d+m$, $E=[I_d\ 0]\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}$ and $E_\theta=[0\ I_m]\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}$. Consider the autonomous augmented system, with components $t,u,\vartheta,C,V,g$,
$$t'=1,\quad \vartheta'=0,\quad u'=f(t,u,\vartheta),\quad C'=\ell(t,u,\vartheta),$$
$$V'=f_u(t,u,\vartheta)V+f_\theta(t,u,\vartheta)E_\theta,$$
$$g'=V^T\ell_u(t,u,\vartheta)^T+E_\theta^T\ell_\theta(t,u,\vartheta)^T.$$
For every admitted local start use $(t_n,x,\theta,0,E,0)$. Suppose application of the same tableau to this augmented system has uniform exact-start defect at most $C_a h^{p+1}$, for an integer $p\ge1$, on a common compact convex augmented tube with positive margin. This is a local augmented-order hypothesis, not a global tangent, adjoint or gradient-error assumption.

Then the actual maps $\Psi_n,L_n$ satisfy all local value, first-derivative, $1+Lh$ derivative-stability, $Mh$ derivative-size, and $Hh$ exact-derivative Lipschitz hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], with constants independent of $n,N$. Subject to that lemma's initial and terminal hypotheses, their actual differentiated graph tangents, exact reverse adjoints, and reduced gradients consequently have order-$p$ global error.

A concrete sufficient instantiation for $1\le p\le4$ is that this augmented vector field is $C^4$ with bounded derivatives through order four on its admitted compact convex tube and the tableau satisfies the coefficient equations through order $p$ in [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]]. Jointly $C^5$ base data $f,\ell$ with bounded derivatives through order five on the base tube are sufficient for this augmented $C^4$ condition. The classical RK4 tableau
$$a_{21}=a_{32}=\tfrac12,\quad a_{43}=1,\quad b=(\tfrac16,\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac16),\quad c=(0,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,1),$$
with all other $a_{ij}=0$, therefore gives the claimed order-four tangent, nodal-adjoint and gradient approximation under these hypotheses. For general $p$, retain the explicit local augmented-defect hypothesis above; no higher-order coefficient theorem is being asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] Explicit RK stages are finite successive compositions. The ordinary chain and product rules differentiate their actual maps.

[F2] The common-tube flow derivative solves the variational equation. Grönwall bounds its solutions uniformly on a fixed finite time interval.

[F3] The order-conditions supplier establishes local order through four for a $C^4$ autonomous augmented field on its stated compact convex tube. The time equation produces the actual stage times because $c_i=\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}$.

[F4] Uniform local defect and one-step Lipschitz stability imply global error for the same augmented method. The preceding local-C1 lemma independently derives the backward nodal-adjoint estimate and the graph-gradient estimate.

[A1] The domain, local flow, derivative, tube, local augmented-defect, initial-data and terminal-data assumptions in the Statement hold. The augmented local tube includes the exact local augmented paths and actual augmented RK stages for all the specified seeds. No tube containment is inferred from a formal order condition alone.

## Proof

1.1 Set $\xi=(x,\theta)$. The exact local solution has $V(t)=D_\xi u(t)$ because $V(t_n)=E$ and its displayed equation is the variational equation, with $D_\xi\theta=E_\theta$. Differentiating the cost integral gives $g(t)=D_\xi C(t)^T$. Thus at the local endpoint,
$$V^+=[D_x\Phi_n\ D_\theta\Phi_n],\qquad g^+=\begin{pmatrix}D_xK_n^T\\D_\theta K_n^T\end{pmatrix}.$$
The flow result and bounded continuous derivatives justify these differentiations uniformly. [F2, A1]

1.2 Differentiate each actual stage, in its explicit order. If $V_i=D_\xi Y_i$, then
$$V_i=E+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}(f_{u,j}V_j+f_{\theta,j}E_\theta),$$
$$D_\xi\Psi_n=E+h\sum_i b_i(f_{u,i}V_i+f_{\theta,i}E_\theta),$$
$$D_\xi L_n^T=h\sum_i b_i(V_i^T\ell_{u,i}^T+E_\theta^T\ell_{\theta,i}^T).$$
These are exactly the $V$ and $g$ outputs obtained by applying the same RK tableau to the augmented system. Its $C$ output is $L_n$ and its $u$ output is $\Psi_n$. Consequently the assumed augmented local defect bounds $\Psi_n-\Phi_n$, $L_n-K_n$, and all four first-derivative differences by constants times $h^{p+1}$. Projection to a component does not increase the Euclidean norm; a matrix Frobenius bound also bounds its operator norm. [F1, A1, step 1.1]

2.1 For a fixed finite tableau, the stage derivative recurrences in step 1.2 give uniform bounds on $D_xY_i,D_\theta Y_i$ by induction, using $h\le h_0$ and the bounded first derivatives of $f$. Here $D_xY_i=I+O(h)$ and $D_\theta Y_i=O(h)$. Substitution into the output derivatives gives
$$D_x\Psi_n=I+O(h),\quad D_\theta\Psi_n=O(h),\quad D_xL_n^T=O(h),\quad D_\theta L_n^T=O(h),$$
uniformly. In particular $\|D_x\Psi_n\|\le1+L_hh$ for a fixed constant $L_h$. The exact variational integral equation gives the same bounds for the exact maps, with $\|D_x\Phi_n\|\le e^{Kh}\le1+Ke^{Kh_0}h$. Enlarging the constants gives the common $L,M$ required by the preceding lemma. [F1, F2, A1]

3.1 The exact maps have the required second-derivative bounds of size $O(h)$. To justify differentiating their variational equations, apply the common-tube $C^1$ flow result to the first variational system: its field is $C^1$ since $f$ is $C^2$, its initial derivative seed is constant, and its variational components remain bounded by [F2]. For coordinate directions $a,b$ of $\xi$, put $W_{ab}=D_{\xi_a}D_{\xi_b}u$. Then
$$W_{ab}'=f_uW_{ab}+D^2_{(u,\theta)}f[(V_a,E_{\theta,a}),(V_b,E_{\theta,b})],\qquad W_{ab}(t_n)=0.$$
The forcing is uniformly bounded, so Grönwall on an interval of length $h$ gives $\|W_{ab}\|\le C h$. Differentiating the cost integral twice produces the integrand
$$D^2_{(u,\theta)}\ell[(V_a,E_{\theta,a}),(V_b,E_{\theta,b})]+\ell_uW_{ab},$$
which is uniformly bounded, and hence $D_\xi^2K_n=O(h)$. Thus $D_\xi^2\Phi_n=O(h)$ and $D_\xi^2K_n=O(h)$. Applying the one-dimensional mean value inequality along each admitted state segment gives Lipschitz constants $Hh$ for $A_n^e,B_n^e,c_n^e,d_n^e$. [F1, F2, A1, step 2.1]

4.1 Steps 1.2–3.1 establish precisely the local hypotheses of the preceding lemma. That lemma now proves the global state, actual graph-tangent, backward nodal-adjoint and gradient bounds. In particular the adjoint conclusion is derived; it is not inserted as an additional hypothesis. [F4, steps 1.2, 2.1, 3.1]

4.2 There is also a direct augmented global-error interpretation. Along a full trajectory append $C'=\ell$ and the column $G'=S^T\ell_u^T+\ell_\theta^T$, with $C(0)=0,G(0)=0$ and $S'=f_uS+f_\theta$. Differentiating the actual stages shows that its numerical step is exactly
$$S^+=A_n^hS+B_n^h,\quad C^+=C+L_n,\quad G^+=G+S^Tc_n^h+d_n^h.$$
The analogous exact step uses the exact maps. On bounded $S$ sets, step 1.2 therefore supplies a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ local defect for $(u,S,C,G)$. Exact $S$ is bounded by Grönwall; numerical $S$ is bounded by the $1+Lh,Mh$ recurrence from step 2.1. The sums defining $C,G$ then bound them uniformly as well. Their stage values are bounded by the same finite-stage induction.

4.3 On a common compact convex augmented tube containing these values and joining stage segments, the $C^1$ augmented field has a derivative bound $K$. For two starting augmented states with difference $\delta$, explicit stage differences obey $\delta_i\le\delta+hK\sum_{j<i}|a_{ij}|\delta_j$. Induction gives $\delta_i\le D_i\delta$, where $D_1=1$ and $D_i=1+h_0K\sum_{j<i}|a_{ij}|D_j$. The output difference is at most $(1+hK\sum_i|b_i|D_i)\delta$. Thus the actual augmented method has one-step stability $1+\Lambda h$. The global-error supplier applies, giving order-$p$ error in the actual tangent and accumulated cost derivative as well. This independently exhibits the augmented local-to-global route; step 4.1 additionally supplies the nodal adjoint. [F4, A1, steps 2.1, 4.2]

5.1 For $p\le4$, apply [F3] to the displayed autonomous augmented field itself. Its derivatives through order four exist and are uniformly bounded under the asserted augmented $C^4$ hypothesis. Joint base $C^5$ regularity is sufficient because its variational components use first derivatives of the base fields. All its exact paths and stages are admitted by [A1]. The source proposition therefore supplies the exact local augmented-defect premise used in step 1.2. This application concerns the differentiated augmented method, rather than just its state projection. [F3, A1, step 1.2]

5.2 For the displayed RK4 tableau the eight coefficient sums, in the order stated in the source proposition, are $1,1/2,1/3,1/6,1/4,1/12,1/8,1/24$. For example $Ac=(0,0,1/4,1/2)$, $Ac^{[2]}=(0,0,1/8,1/4)$, and $A^2c=(0,0,0,1/4)$, which verify the mixed sums directly. Hence step 5.1 applies with $p=4$. No division by an individual $b_i$ or internal-stage adjoint order condition occurs in this argument. [F3, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

The concrete RK4 case uses the actual C4 augmented-field premise of the existing order proposition; base C5 is an explicit sufficient condition. Generic p retains a genuine local augmented-defect hypothesis.

## Statement

Let $J$ and $J_h$ be the continuous and finite state-step objectives of [[thm-continuous-ode-adjoint-gradient-formula]] and [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]], respectively, and put $h=T/N$. Let $q(t,u,p)=D_\theta\ell(t,u,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u,\theta)^Tp$ be the continuous running-gradient vector, evaluated on its exact state and adjoint as $q(t):=q(t,u(t),p(t))$. Suppose the exact and numerical state/adjoint pairs lie in a common tube and
$$\max_n\bigl(\|u_n-u(t_n)\|_2+\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\bigr)\le C_xh^p.$$
For the state part of this bound, it is sufficient that the hypotheses of [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]] hold with a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ exact-start defect; the coefficient conditions of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]] supply that defect for an explicit Runge--Kutta method of order $p\le4$ under that item's $C^4$ and common-tube assumptions. No cited state-error result supplies the adjoint part, which is an independent hypothesis here. Write $b$ and $b_h$ for the column initial/terminal contribution vectors in the continuous and discrete gradient formulas. Assume the discrete running-gradient terms admit vectors $\widehat q_n$ and nonnegative weights $w_n$, $0\le n\le N$, with
$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$
The weighted discrete representation is an explicit premise; it is not implied by the generic finite state-step adjoint recursion. Suppose
$$\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n,u_n,p_n)\|_2\le C_dh^p,\qquad \|b_h-b\|_2\le C_bh^p,$$
and that the same weights give the quadrature $Q_h(q)=\sum_{n=0}^Nw_nq(t_n)$ satisfying
$$\left\|Q_h(q)-\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt\right\|_2\le C_Qh^p.$$
If $q$ is Lipschitz in $(u,p)$ on the common tube with constant $L_q$ in the sum norm, then
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le\bigl(C_b+T(C_d+L_qC_x)+C_Q\bigr)h^p.$$
The adjoint, derivative-data and quadrature hypotheses are separate from state accuracy; without them the state estimate alone gives no gradient error conclusion.

There is also the following independent method-consistency conclusion. Under the local $C^1$ step-and-cost consistency, derivative stability, derivative Lipschitz, initial-data, terminal-derivative and tube hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], the actual numerical graph satisfies
$$\max_n\|D_\theta u_n-D_\theta u(t_n)\|_2\le C_Sh^p,\qquad \max_n\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\le C_Ph^p,$$
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le C_Gh^p,$$
with that lemma's explicit constants, together with its state bound. These conclusions derive the global tangent and adjoint errors from local map errors. They do not assume the preceding global state/adjoint bound or weighted representation.

In particular, [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] supplies these local hypotheses for the actual explicit RK state map and the cost using the same tableau, under its common-tube, base $C^2$, and local augmented-order hypotheses. For $p\le4$, its augmented $C^4$ hypothesis and the existing coefficient conditions suffice; jointly $C^5$ base data are an explicit sufficient smoothness condition, and its displayed classical RK4 tableau gives a concrete order-four instance. Generic $p$ is retained through its genuine local augmented-order hypothesis. This branch permits negative or zero RK weights and makes no internal-stage adjoint accuracy claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** In the weighted conclusion, the stated continuous and discrete objectives, exact adjoint formulas, uniform state/adjoint error bound, derivative-data perturbation bound, quadrature bound, and common compact tube. In the method-consistency conclusion, the actual step and cost maps and the separate local hypotheses of the two cited local lemmas.

[F1] [[thm-continuous-ode-adjoint-gradient-formula]]: the continuous gradient is the initial/terminal contribution plus $\int_0^T q(t)\,dt$.

[F2] [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]: the discrete gradient is the corresponding initial/terminal contribution plus the reverse-mode sum of the discrete running derivative terms.

[F3] [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]]: the common-tube, uniform local-defect, one-step stability and initial-error hypotheses imply the stated uniform state-error bound.

[F4] [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]]: for an explicit tableau satisfying the stated coefficient equations through $p\le4$, a $C^4$ vector field on the common compact tube has uniform exact-start defect $O(h^{p+1})$. It supplies a state local-defect premise only when applied just to the state field; it makes no adjoint or tangent error claim by itself.

[F5] [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]] derives global state, actual tangent, nodal-adjoint and gradient errors by comparing the exact-flow and numerical graphs under its local value/first-derivative hypotheses.

[F6] [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] identifies derivatives of actual RK stages and matching cost quadrature with the same augmented method, verifies the local hypotheses of [F5], and instantiates local augmented order through four using [F4] on the augmented field.

[A1] For the weighted conclusion, the constants $C_b,C_x,C_d,C_Q,L_q$ are independent of $h$, and all error, quadrature and derivative-data hypotheses in that part of the Statement hold.

[A2] For the independent method-consistency conclusion, every hypothesis of [F5] holds, or is supplied by [F6] together with the initial and terminal hypotheses of [F5]. No global adjoint-error estimate is included in [A2].

## Proof

1.1 If the stated explicit Runge--Kutta conditions are used for the state field, [F4] supplies the exact-start defect required by [F3]. Under the stated stability, common-tube and initial-error hypotheses, [F3] gives the state part of the asserted $C_xh^p$ bound; the adjoint part in the weighted conclusion remains the separately assumed bound. [F3, F4, A1]

2.1 By [F1], [F2], and the explicit weighted representation in the Statement, the two gradients are their respective endpoint terms plus, respectively, the weighted sum of $\widehat q_n$ and the integral of $q$. At each node, insert and subtract $q(t_n,u_n,p_n)$. The derivative-data assumption and Lipschitz bound give $\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n)\|_2\le(C_d+L_qC_x)h^p$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Since $w_n\ge0$ and $\sum_nw_n=T$, the node-data perturbation contributes at most $T(C_d+L_qC_x)h^p$. The exact-integrand quadrature error contributes at most $C_Qh^p$, and the endpoint difference at most $C_bh^p$. The Euclidean triangle inequality gives the displayed weighted bound. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Independently assume [A2]. Apply [F5] to the actual maps defining $J_h$ and the exact interval flow and running-cost maps defining $J$. Its forward recurrences give state and tangent errors, its backward recurrence gives the nodal-adjoint error, and its graph-gradient comparison gives the stated $C_Gh^p$ bound. This argument uses no weighted decomposition. [A2, F5]

4.2 For the RK specialization, [F6] differentiates the actual finite stages, proves the local derivative-size and Lipschitz bounds, and obtains the needed local $C^1$ consistency from augmented local order. Its application of [F4] to the augmented field verifies this order for $p\le4$ under the actual augmented smoothness and tube assumptions. Its RK4 coefficient calculation supplies the concrete fourth-order instance. Therefore step 4.1 applies. [A2, F4, F6, step 4.1] ∎

## Statement

Use the implicit Runge–Kutta residual $G(Y)=Y-\mathbf1\otimes u-h(A\otimes I_d)F(Y)$ from [[def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations]] on a convex open neighborhood of an invariant stage ball. Suppose $F$ is $C^1$ there and $\|D_YF(Y)Z\|_{\infty,2}\le L\|Z\|_{\infty,2}$ for every $Y$ in the ball and every block vector $Z$. If $q=h\|A\|_\infty L<1$, then $D_YG(Y)$ is invertible at every point of the selected stage branch. The contraction hypotheses of [[lem-small-step-implicit-rk-branch-and-residual-error]] provide existence and uniqueness of the root in that ball; this lemma supplies nonsingularity for implicit differentiation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite-dimensional stage space, implicit Runge–Kutta residual, selected invariant ball, $C^1$ map $F$, derivative bound $L$ on the ball, and $q<1$.

[F1] The stage residual is $G(Y)=Y-\mathbf1\otimes u-h(A\otimes I_d)F(Y)$; a selected stage root satisfies $G(Y)=0$ ([[def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations]]).

[F2] If $F$ is Lipschitz on the invariant ball with constant $L$ and $h\|A\|_\infty L<1$, the stage fixed-point map has a unique root on the prescribed branch ([[lem-small-step-implicit-rk-branch-and-residual-error]]).

[F3] A vector-valued function continuous on $[0,1]$, differentiable on $(0,1)$, and with Euclidean derivative norm at most $M$ has endpoint difference at most $M$ ([[thm-mean-value-inequality]]). The chain rule differentiates a $C^1$ map along a segment ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

[F4] For a linear map on a finite-dimensional vector space, $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{im}T$ ([[thm-rank-nullity]]).

## Proof

1.1 Let $Y,W$ belong to the invariant ball. Its convexity puts $Y+t(W-Y)$ in the ball for $0\le t\le1$. For each block $i$, the curve $\gamma_i(t)=F_i(Y+t(W-Y))$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and differentiable inside because $F$ is $C^1$ on an open neighborhood. Its derivative obeys
$$\|\gamma_i'(t)\|_2\le\|D_YF(Y+t(W-Y))(W-Y)\|_{\infty,2}\le L\|W-Y\|_{\infty,2}.$$
Apply [F3] to each block and take the maximum. This gives $\|F(W)-F(Y)\|_{\infty,2}\le L\|W-Y\|_{\infty,2}$ using only the derivative bound on the ball. Hence [F2] applies with its invariant-ball hypotheses and the selected root exists uniquely. [given, F2, F3]

1.2 Differentiating [F1] with respect to $Y$ gives $D_YG=I-h(A\otimes I_d)D_YF$. If $D_YG\,Z=0$, the block row-sum norm and the derivative bound imply
$$\|Z\|_{\infty,2}\le h\|A\|_\infty L\|Z\|_{\infty,2}=q\|Z\|_{\infty,2}.$$
Since $q<1$, this forces $Z=0$; thus the square finite-dimensional map $D_YG$ has trivial kernel. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F4], a linear map on the stage space has rank equal to its dimension when its kernel has dimension zero. Therefore $D_YG$ is onto as well as one-to-one, hence invertible. This holds at every point of the prescribed branch ball. [F4, step 1.2] ∎
proposed_items.proof_explanation: Proof-only repair; the Statement is unchanged. Removes the unsupported stronger neighborhood derivative assumption. A blockwise segment argument proves the needed Lipschitz bound with exactly the stated block norm and constant.

## Example

For $u'=\theta u$ on two intervals of length $\tau>0$, define shooting nodes $z_0,z_1,z_2$ and residuals $R_0=z_0-a$, $R_1=z_1-e^{\tau\theta}z_0$, and $R_2=z_2-e^{\tau\theta}z_1$. This uses the exact parameterized ODE flow covered locally by [[lem-parameter-ode-flow-tangent-on-common-tube]]. On the shooting solution set, take terminal objective $J=z_2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $a\in\mathbb R$, $\tau>0$, the two exact-flow intervals, and the finite shooting graph.

[F1] The parameterized ODE flow has its variational tangent when its uniqueness and common-tube hypotheses hold ([[lem-parameter-ode-flow-tangent-on-common-tube]]).

[F2] The reverse recursion computes the exact gradient of a finite state-step objective ([[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]).

[F3] The exponential is smooth with derivative equal to itself, is positive, satisfies $e^{-x}=1/e^x$, and is increasing ([[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]).

[F4] The chain and product rules differentiate the displayed functions; a continuous function on an interval with zero interior derivative is constant ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]).

## Verification

1.1 The function $u(t)=e^{\theta t}s$ satisfies $u'=\theta u$ and $u(0)=s$. Conversely, for any solution $v$ with this initial value, the product and chain rules give $(e^{-\theta t}v(t))'=0$. By [F4] this product is constantly $s$ on its solution interval, and positivity and the reciprocal identity in [F3] imply $v(t)=e^{\theta t}s$. Thus the displayed solution exists globally and is unique. [F3, F4]

1.2 Verify the actual common-tube hypotheses locally at any $(s_*,\theta_*)$. Fix $\varepsilon,\delta,\eta>0$ and restrict the parameters to $|s-s_*|<\varepsilon$, $|\theta-\theta_*|<\delta$. For $-\eta\le t\le\tau+\eta$,
$$|e^{\theta t}s|\le B:=(|s_*|+\varepsilon)\exp((|\theta_*|+\delta)(\tau+\eta)).$$
Treat $(s,\theta)$ as the flow parameter, with initial map $(s,\theta)\mapsto s$ and field $(t,u,s,\theta)\mapsto\theta u$ on $\mathbb R^4$. The bounded convex open set
$$(-\eta,\tau+\eta)\times(-B-1,B+1)\times(s_*-2\varepsilon,s_*+2\varepsilon)\times(\theta_*-2\delta,\theta_*+2\delta)$$
has compact closure inside that field's domain and contains all these trajectories for $0\le t\le\tau$ and the restricted parameters. The field and initial map are $C^1$. Step 1.1 supplies existence and uniqueness, so [F1] applies. Each shooting interval uses this same argument with its own initial node; since there are two intervals, a common finite bound may also be taken. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

1.3 The exact interval map is therefore $\Phi_\tau(s,\theta)=e^{\tau\theta}s$. Differentiate the residuals with respect to $(z_0,z_1,z_2)$ and $\theta$, writing $E=e^{\tau\theta}$:
$$D_zR=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-E&1&0\\0&-E&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_\theta R=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-\tau E z_0\\-\tau E z_1\end{pmatrix}.$$
The state Jacobian is lower bidiagonal, and the parameter column contains the two local flow sensitivities. [F3, F4, steps 1.1, 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Solving $R=0$ gives $z_0=a$, $z_1=Ea$, and $z_2=E^2a$. Direct differentiation yields $D_\theta z_2=2\tau E^2a$. The discrete adjoint for the two flow steps seeds $p_2=1$, then gives $p_1=E$ and $p_0=E^2$; its parameter sum is $\tau E z_0p_1+\tau E z_1p_2=2\tau E^2a$. Thus the reverse gradient agrees with the differentiated shooting solution. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.3, algebra] ∎
proposed_items.proof_explanation: The Example interface and computed residual/gradient remain unchanged. The repair proves uniqueness by an integrating factor and explicitly verifies a finite common tube for initial-state and coefficient parameters before invoking the flow supplier.

## Example

Take the scalar discrete model $x_0(\theta)=\theta$, $x_1=2x_0$, and $x_2=3x_1$. Instantiate the strong-constraint objective of [[alg-four-dimensional-variational-assimilation]] with $T=2$, $d_0=d_1=d_2=p_1=p_2=1$, $U_0=U_1=U_2=\mathbb R$, model maps $\Psi_0(x)=2x$ and $\Psi_1(x)=3x$, and observation maps $G_1=G_2=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb R}$. Choose $m_b=y_1=y_2=0$ and the scalar positive-definite covariance matrices $B=\Gamma_1=\Gamma_2=[1]$. The decision variable is the initial state $x_0=\theta$; there are no weak-constraint model-error penalties. The objective is exactly
$$J(\theta)=\tfrac12x_0^2+\tfrac12x_1^2+\tfrac12x_2^2.$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite scalar state-step graph, identity observation maps, unit positive-definite covariances, strong-constraint objective, and exact-real arithmetic.

[F1] The reverse recursion for a finite $C^1$ state-step objective is its exact gradient ([[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]).

[F2] The strong-constraint variational assimilation objective contains a background penalty and observation-misfit terms along the generated model trajectory ([[alg-four-dimensional-variational-assimilation]]). The stated linear maps are $C^1$ on their open domains and the selected scalar covariances are positive definite, so that objective is admissible.

## Verification

1.1 Direct substitution gives $x_1=2\theta$ and $x_2=6\theta$, so $J(\theta)=\frac12(1+4+36)\theta^2=\frac{41}{2}\theta^2$ and $J'(\theta)=41\theta$. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 The terminal adjoint seed is $p_2=x_2=6\theta$. The reverse recursion [F1] gives $p_1=x_1+3p_2=20\theta$ and $p_0=x_0+2p_1=41\theta$. Since $Dx_0/D\theta=1$, the adjoint gradient is $p_0=41\theta$, agreeing with the direct derivative. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

This page separates derivatives of a finite computational graph from derivatives of the exact ODE flow. It gives the continuous and exact finite-graph adjoint formulas. Local value and first-derivative consistency of the actual state and running-cost maps, together with uniform derivative stability and common-tube hypotheses, yield order-$p$ state, tangent, nodal-adjoint and gradient bounds. Differentiating actual explicit Runge–Kutta stages and the matching cost quadrature supplies this local consistency from augmented local order; the stated augmented smoothness and coefficient conditions give concrete instances through order four, including RK4. A separate weighted perturbation theorem retains explicit state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint and same-weight quadrature hypotheses. State accuracy alone does not establish gradient accuracy. Implicit Runge–Kutta sensitivities apply to a selected nonsingular algebraic stage branch, not to a stopped stage iteration.

For elliptic equations, the reduced gradient uses the transposed variational adjoint. The finite-element error budget is restricted to conforming state and adjoint approximations and keeps derivative-data defects separate from state and adjoint errors. An $L^2$ rate additionally needs dual approximation and $L^2$-bounded parameter derivative maps. The parabolic formula is conditional on differentiable state and adjoint solutions; the finite-element estimate retains the full time-dependent Ritz residual derivative $P_h'(t)u(t)+P_h(t)u'(t)-u'(t)$. The QR identity concerns exact finite-time tangent-volume change and does not assert an infinite-time Lyapunov exponent.
